CORRECT AS ABSENT, triaged 2026-09-21. Android says 'switch to an end-to-end encrypted model on near.ai' or 'end-to-end encryption is available on near.ai' instead, from EncryptedModelCTA (ported at 79dde59, which is AFTER the sha this audit reads TrustLadderView+None at). That was a fix, not a rewording: the iOS string here read 'choose an end-to-end encrypted model' from an NVIDIA chat and opened a list of near.ai models with no provider named, whenever a near.ai setup existed — keyed or not. The two Android strings name near.ai and gate on whether a usable key exists. Restoring the iOS wording would restore the bug.

rows.ios: copy this into your terminal to re-verify on your own machine, with your own fresh nonces
rows.why: REWORDED, triaged 2026-09-21. Android's section is 'verify it yourself' / 'the script embeds this session's attested values and re-fetches fresh proofs to compare — on your own machine. don't take our word for it.' Same two claims as iOS's 're-check the live service yourself' + 'copy this into your terminal … with your own fresh nonces': it runs on your machine, and the proofs are fresh rather than replayed. Not aligning them, because the Android wording names what the script DOES; if one side should move it is iOS, and that is their call.

rows.ios: the key is stored in the ios keychain, not in teemoon's own files
rows.why: PLATFORM, triaged 2026-09-21. Android says the same sentence with the right noun — 'the android keystore' / 'the keystore on this device' / 'written to the keystore'. Saying 'keychain' on Android would name a thing the OS does not have, and the sentence exists to tell the user WHERE their key is; getting the place wrong is worse than saying nothing. See AddEditProviderScreen.kt and AppSettingsScreens.kt.
